Z1 Surveys

Screening, admission checklist, demographics, and trait and state questionnaires from the 25 ProPELL surveys, administered via LimeSurvey.
Author

Maik Bieleke et al.

Published

20 November, 2026

Overview

The survey data combine the 25 LimeSurvey surveys of the study: one screening survey and the weekly surveys, completed online or in the laboratory. In LimeSurvey, the surveys were named after the week and the setting, for example s00 (screening), s08o (week 8, online), and s12l (week 12, laboratory). In the processed data, tp replaces these names.

Test phases: p0 (screening), p1 (pre), p2 (post), p3 (follow-up), and the study weeks w02 to w21. See the study timeline.

Dataset Content One row is Key Rows Variables
svyscrp Screening Participant id 75 17
svyadmp Admission checklist Shuffled response set (not a person) none 75 40

svytrts Trait questionnaires Participant in a test phase id, tp 225 617
svystas State questionnaires Participant in a study week id, tp 1,500 82

Code Meaning

ipaq6IPAQ-SF 6 Months

  • Description
  • Distribution
  • Statistics
  • Reference

“We are interested in finding out what types of physical activities you perform in your everyday life. The following questions refer to the time you have spent on physical activity during an average week over the past 6 months. Please answer all questions (even if you do not consider yourself an active person). Please include activities performed as part of your work, in your home and garden, to get from place to place, and during your leisure time for recreation, fitness, and sport. In the following, think about all your vigorous and moderate activities during an average week over the past 6 months. Vigorous activities refer to activities that require strong physical effort and make you breathe much harder than normal. Moderate activities refer to activities that require moderate physical effort and make you breathe somewhat harder than normal.”

Admission checklist

Dataset svyadmp, one row per shuffled response set (no participant ID). The admission checklist was part of the screening survey. It is kept separate to avoid re-identification: responses are not linked to participant IDs, and each variable was shuffled independently. The data describe the sample as a whole, but no row describes a real person.

  • Description
  • Statistics

Indicator for dedicated test phases (p0, p1, p2, or p3) and study weeks (w04 to w20)

checkAdmission checklist

  • Description
  • Values
  • Distribution
  • Statistics

“In this part of the screening, we ask you for health-related information. Even if the connection to health is not immediately apparent for all questions, this information is important to determine whether you can participate in the measurement procedures of the ProPELL study. It is therefore important that you answer all questions thoroughly and truthfully. For some questions, if you answer “yes,” you will be asked to provide additional details. Please provide these details as precisely as possible.”

Variable Label Prompt
check01 Mental disorder status "Are you currently suffering from a mental disorder?"
check02 Physical illness status "Are you currently suffering from an acute physical illness?"
check02d Specification of physical illness "What illness are you suffering from?"
check03 Chronic illness status "Do you suffer from a chronic illness?"
check03d Specification of chronic illness "What chronic illness are you suffering from?"
check04 History of neurological disorder "Do you suffer from a neurological disorder? (e.g. epilepsy, stroke, Parkinson’s disease)"

Gaspard et al. (2017)

aeqAchievement Emotions Questionnaire - Sports and Exercise (AEQ-SE)

  • Description
  • Distribution
  • Statistics
  • Reference
  • Items
  • Values
  • Scale

Directions: “The following questions examine your emotional experiences during sport and exercise. They are organized into three blocks—your emotions before, during, and after sport and exercise. Please first recall some typical situations in which you were physically active before answering the questions. Here, sport is defined as any form of physical activity performed for its own sake; that is, sport is performed for the purpose of the physical activity itself. This includes both competitive sport and recreational sport. The physical activity is goal-directed. The goals pursued through sport can vary widely, for example striving to improve one’s body or abilities, the desire to improve health, comparing one’s performance with oneself or others in competition, social motives, etc. There are also many different contexts in which sport can take place: outdoors (e.g., jogging or on a soccer field), in a fitness studio, in a yoga studio, alone or with others, etc. Typical physical characteristics during sport may include sweating, accelerated breathing, a faster heartbeat, or muscle fatigue. As diverse as the forms of sport can be, so too are the terms used to describe physical activity in this context. In the following questions, different terms such as “sport,” “training,” or “workout” are used. These terms should be considered synonymous.

  • Before exercise. Exercise can evoke different emotions. This part of the questionnaire refers to emotions you may experience BEFORE an exercise session. Please read each statement carefully and, using the statements below, indicate how you typically feel before an exercise session.
  • During exercise. This part of the questionnaire refers to emotions you may experience DURING an exercise session. Using the statements below, please indicate how you typically feel during an exercise session.
  • After exercise. This part of the questionnaire refers to emotions you may experience AFTER an exercise session. Using the statements below, please indicate how you typically feel after an exercise session.”

psdqPhysical Self-Description Questionnaire (PSDQ)

  • Description
  • Distribution
  • Statistics
  • Reference
  • Items
  • Values
  • Scale

Directions: “The following statements concern your body awareness and how you would describe yourself in relation to your body. Please read each statement and choose a response.”

Variable Scale Prompt
psdq01 Coordination "I feel confident when doing coordinated movements."
psdq02 Competence "Other people think that I am good at sports."
psdq03 Flexibility "I'm quite good at bending, twisting, and turning my body."
psdq04 Endurance "I can run a long way without stopping."
psdq05 Coordination "Controlling movements of my body comes easily to me."
psdq06 Competence "I am good at most sports."
psdq07 Stength "I have a lot of power in my body."
psdq08 Flexibility "My body is flexible."
psdq09 Endurance "I would do well in a test of physical endurance and stamina."
psdq10 Coordination "I am good at coordinated movements."
psdq11 Competence "Most sports are easy for me."
psdq12 Stength "I am stronger than most people my age."
psdq13* Flexibility "My body is stiff and inflexible. "
psdq14 Endurance "I could jog 5 kilometers without stopping."
psdq15 Coordination "I can perform movements smoothly in most physical activities."
psdq16 Competence "I have good sport skills."
psdq17* Stength "I am weak and have no muscles."
psdq18 Flexibility "My body parts bend and move in most directions well."
psdq19 Endurance "I think I could run a long way without getting tired."
psdq20 Coordination "I find my body handles coordinated movements with ease."
psdq21 Competence "I am better at sports than most of my friends."
psdq22 Stength "I would do well in a test of strength."
psdq23 Flexibility "I think I am flexible enough for most sports."
psdq24 Endurance "I can be physically active for a long period of time without getting tired."
psdq25 Coordination "I am graceful and coordinated when I do sports and activities."
psdq26 Competence "I play sports well."
psdq27 Stength "I am good at lifting heavy objects."
psdq28 Flexibility "I think I would perform well on a test measuring flexibility."

Schüler et al. (2023)

probctProactive Behavior Change Techniques (ProBCT)

  • Description
  • Distribution
  • Statistics
  • Reference
  • Items
  • Values
  • Scale

Directions: “The following statements describe strategies that people commonly use to change their exercise and physical activity behavior. Please indicate the extent to which you use these strategies for your own exercise and physical activity goals. Strategies I use to achieve my exercise and physical activity goals:”

Variable Scale Prompt
probct01 Behavior-Health Link "I search for information about the relationship between sport and activity and health (e.g. on the Internet, physician)."
probct02 Costs and Benefits "I weigh the benefits and costs of sport and activity in terms of health outcomes."
probct03 Social Approval "I consider whether or not other people like my changed sport and activity behavior."
probct04 Intention Formation "I explicitly stated my desire to sport and activity as a goal (e.g., "I want to exercise more," "I will exercise next week")."
probct05 Barrier Identification "I identify obstacles that interfere with my sport and activity behavior and look for solutions to overcome them."
probct06 Self-Encouragement "I encourage myself to exert effort and perform (e.g., encouragement, reward)."
probct07 Graded Tasks "I start with easy tasks and increase the difficulty until I reach my sport and activity goal."
probct08 Behavior Instruction "I look for information on how to best perform the sport and activity behavior (e.g., on the Internet, from friends)."
probct09 Expert Models "I am looking for experts (coaches, videos) to show me how to properly perform the sport and activity behavior."
probct10 Goals and Plans "I make detailed plans for my sports and activity behavior (e.g., where, when, how, and with whom)."
probct11 Review and Rethink "I review and rethink my set sport and activity goal (e.g., Does it fit me? Is it realistic?)."
probct12 Self-Monitoring "I document my sport and activity behavior (e.g. diary, weekly log)."
probct13 Goal Feedback "I match my actual sport and activity behavior with my set goals and use this as feedback."
probct14 Self-reward "I reward myself for achieving specific behavioral and subgoals (e.g., going to the movies for regular exercise participation; eating well for reaching step count)."
probct15 Cues and Prompts "I use cues from my environment to remind me to do sport and activity (e.g., fixed time, reminders)."
probct16 Behavioral Contract "I make my sport and activity goal public and binding (e.g., tell my partner or friends; write it down)."
probct17 Practice and Repetition "I practice and repeat behaviors that bring me closer to my sport and activity goal."
probct18 Follow-up Prompts "I take precautions to remind myself to perform the sport and activity behavior in the future (e.g., automatic reminders, other reminders)."
probct19 Social Comparison "I seek opportunities to compare myself with others in my sport and activity behavior."
probct20 Social Support "I look for social support to achieve my sport and activity goal (e.g., how can others support me?)."
probct21 Role Model "I try to be a role model for others with my sport and activity behavior and to positively influence their behavior."
probct22 Self-Talk "I use self-instructions to motivate me to achieve my sport and activity goal (e.g., mental encouragement, concrete instructions)."
probct23 Relapse Prevention "I identify situations in which I could fall back into a sedentary behavior and try to avoid them."
probct24 Stress Management "I specifically try to regulate stress (e.g., progressive muscle relaxation)."
probct25 Self-Motivation "I use self-motivating statements to minimize possible inner resistance to the sport and activity goal (e.g., "I can do it","Come on now, pull yourself together")."
probct26 Time Management "I plan my time so that my sport and activity behavior fits into everyday life."

1Strongly disagree 2Disagree 3Somewhat disagree 4Neither nor 5Somewhat agree 6Agree 7Strongly agree

Directions: “Please read the following statements and indicate, using the response scale, how strongly you agree with them. There are no right or wrong answers. Respond quickly and choose the answers that best describe what you believe and how you feel.”

Variable Scale Prompt
pretieq01* Tolerance "Feeling tired during exercise is my signal to slow down or stop."
pretieq02* Preference "I would rather work out at low intensity levels for a long duration than at high-intensity levels for a short duration."
pretieq03* Tolerance "During exercise, if my muscles begin to burn excessively or if I find myself breathing very hard, it is time for me to ease off."
pretieq04* Preference "I’d rather go slow during my workout, even if that means taking more time."
pretieq05 Tolerance "While exercising, I try to keep going even after I feel exhausted."
pretieq06 Preference "I would rather have a short, intense workout than a long, low-intensity workout."
pretieq07 Tolerance "I block out the feeling of fatigue when exercising."
pretieq08* Preference "When I exercise, I usually prefer a slow, steady pace."
pretieq09* Tolerance "I’d rather slow down or stop when a workout starts to get too tough."
pretieq10 Preference "Exercising at a low intensity does not appeal to me at all."
pretieq11 Tolerance "Fatigue is the last thing that affects when I stop a workout; I have a goal and stop only when I reach it."
pretieq12* Preference "While exercising, I prefer activities that are slow-paced and do not require much exertion."
pretieq13* Tolerance "When my muscles start burning during exercise, I usually ease off some."
pretieq14 Preference "The faster and harder the workout, the more pleasant I feel."
pretieq15 Tolerance "I always push through muscle soreness and fatigue when working out."
pretieq16 Preference "Low-intensity exercise is boring."

Variables with * have been reverse-coded.

Directions: “The following statements refer to sports activities that are physically demanding. Please read each statement and indicate the extent to which it generally applies to you.”

Variable Prompt
vope01 "I greatly enjoy sports activities that require physical effort."
vope02 "I prefer physically effortful sports activities to those that can be done without much effort."
vope03* "I find it hard to get enthusiastic about new sports activities if they involve physical effort."
vope04 "The notion of physically exerting myself in sports appeals to me."
vope05* "I physically exert myself in sports only as much as I absolutely have to."
vope06* "I try to anticipate and avoid situations in sports where there is a good chance that I will have to physically exert myself."
vope07* "Other things equal, I would rather do sports activities with less physical effort."
vope08* "A sports activity feels like a burden as soon as I start thinking about the physical effort involved."
vope09 "I enjoy physically exerting myself in a sports activity even when it will have no effect on the result."
vope10 "When I know that a sports activity is going to involve physical effort, I look forward to it, even if I do not know what exactly it involves."

Variables with * have been reverse-coded.

1Does not apply at all 2Does not apply 3Rather does not apply 4Neither nor 5Rather applies 6Applies 7Fully applies

Directions: “Below you will find a series of statements. Please select the statement that best describes your situation over the past 7 days. Please note: These questions were developed for comparisons across different age groups (including older age). Therefore, not all statements may seem applicable to your current life situation. Nevertheless, please select the statement that fits best in each case.”

Variable Scale Prompt
aqol01 Coping "How much energy do you have to do the things you want to do? I am …"
aqol02 Relationships "How often do you feel socially excluded or left out?"
aqol03 Independent Living "How easy or difficult is it for you to get around by yourself outside your place of residence (eg. to go shopping, visiting)?"
aqol04 Relationships "Does your health affect your role in your community (eg. residential, sporting, church or cultural activities)?"
aqol05 Mental Health "How often do you feel sad?"
aqol06 Pain "How often do you experience serious pain? I experience it…"
aqol07 Self-Worth "How much confidence do you have in yourself?"

aqol09 Relationships "Does your health affect your relationship with your family?"
aqol10 Relationships "How satisfying are your close relationships (family and friends)?"
aqol11 Senses "How well do you communicate with others (talking, signing, texting, being understood by others and understanding them)?"
aqol12 Mental Health "How often do you have trouble sleeping?"
aqol13 Self-Worth "How often do you feel worthless?"
aqol14 Mental Health "How often do you feel angry?"

aqol18 Mental Health "How often did you feel worried in the last seven days?"
aqol19 Independent Living "How difficult is it for you to wash, toilet, dress yourself, eat or care for your appearance?"

aqol21 Coping "How much do you feel you can cope with life’s problems?"
aqol22 Pain "How much pain or discomfort do you experience?"

erqEmotion Regulation Questionnaire (ERQ)

  • Description
  • Distribution
  • Statistics
  • Reference
  • Items
  • Values
  • Scale

Directions: “We would like to ask you some questions about your emotions. We are interested in how you control or regulate your emotions. Two aspects of your emotions are of particular interest. On the one hand, this concerns your emotional experience, that is, what you feel internally. On the other hand, it concerns emotional expression, that is, how you express your emotions outwardly through words, gestures, or behavior. Although some of the questions may sound quite similar, they differ in important ways. Please answer the questions using the response options provided.”

Variable Scale Prompt
erq01 Reappraisal "When I want to feel more positive emotion (such as joy or amusement), I change what I’m thinking about."
erq02 Suppression "I keep my emotions to myself."
erq03 Reappraisal "When I want to feel less negative emotion (such as sadness or anger), I change what I’m thinking about."
erq04 Suppression "When I am feeling positive emotions, I am careful not to express them."
erq05 Reappraisal "When I’m faced with a stressful situation, I make myself think about it in a way that helps me stay calm."
erq06 Suppression "I control my emotions by not expressing them."
erq07 Reappraisal "When I want to feel more positive emotion, I change the way I’m thinking about the situation."
erq08 Reappraisal "I control my emotions by changing the way I think about the situation I’m in."
erq09 Suppression "When I am feeling negative emotions, I make sure not to express them."
erq10 Reappraisal "When I want to feel less negative emotion, I change the way I’m thinking about the situation."

1Does not apply at all 2 3 4Neutral 5 6 7Fully applies

rsqdResponse Style Questionnaire (RSQ)

  • Description
  • Distribution
  • Statistics
  • Reference
  • Items
  • Values
  • Scale

Directions: “People think and behave differently when they feel sad or down. Please indicate for each of the following statements whether you “almost never,” “sometimes,” “often,” or “almost always” think or do this when you feel sad, down, or depressed. Please indicate what you usually do when you feel sad or down, not what you think you should do.”

Variable Scale Prompt
rsqd01 Self-focused rumination "When I feel sad or down ... I think about how alone I feel."
rsqd02 Symptom-focused rumination "When I feel sad or down ... I think, "I won’t be able to do my work because I feel so bad.""
rsqd03 Symptom-focused rumination "When I feel sad or down ... I think about how exhausted I feel."
rsqd04 Symptom-focused rumination "When I feel sad or down ... I think about how hard it is to concentrate."
rsqd05 Distraction "When I feel sad or down ... I try to find something positive about the situation or something I have learned from it."
rsqd06 Distraction "When I feel sad or down ... I think, "I will do something now to make myself feel better.""
rsqd07 Distraction "When I feel sad or down ... I help someone else with something to distract myself."
rsqd08 Symptom-focused rumination "When I feel sad or down ... I think about how passive and unmotivated I am."
rsqd09 Distraction "When I feel sad or down ... I tell myself that these feelings will not last."
rsqd10 Symptom-focused rumination "When I feel sad or down ... I think about how I don’t seem to feel anything at all anymore."
rsqd11 Symptom-focused rumination "When I feel sad or down ... I think, "Why can’t I get going?""
rsqd12 Symptom-focused rumination "When I feel sad or down ... I think, "Why do I always react this way?""
rsqd13 Distraction "When I feel sad or down ... I go to a favorite place to distract myself from my feelings."
rsqd14 Distraction "When I feel sad or down ... I think, "I will now focus on something other than how I feel.""
rsqd15 Distraction "When I feel sad or down ... I do something that has made me feel better in the past."
rsqd16 Self-focused rumination "When I feel sad or down ... I think about a past situation and wish it had gone better."
rsqd17 Distraction "When I feel sad or down ... I think, "I will go out now and have some fun.""
rsqd18 Symptom-focused rumination "When I feel sad or down ... I think about how I don’t feel strong enough to do anything."
rsqd19 Self-focused rumination "When I feel sad or down ... I reflect on my personality and try to understand why I am depressed."
rsqd20 Self-focused rumination "When I feel sad or down ... I go somewhere where I can be alone to think about my feelings."
rsqd21 Self-focused rumination "When I feel sad or down ... I listen to sad music."
rsqd22 Self-focused rumination "When I feel sad or down ... I withdraw and think about the reasons why I feel so sad."
rsqd23 Self-focused rumination "When I feel sad or down ... I try to understand myself by focusing on my depressive feelings."

1Almost never 2Sometimes 3Often 4Almost always

  • Distribution
  • Statistics

“We are interested in finding out what types of physical activities you perform in your daily life. The following questions refer to the time you spent on physical activity during the last 7 days. Please answer all questions (even if you do not consider yourself an active person). Please include activities as part of your work, in the house and garden, to get from one place to another, and in your leisure time for recreation, fitness, and sport. In the following, think about all your strenuous and moderate activities during the past 7 days. Strenuous activities refer to activities that require hard physical effort and make you breathe much harder than normal. Moderate activities refer to activities that require moderate physical effort and make you breathe somewhat harder than normal.”

Based on Duckworth et al. (2016) and Hennecke et al. (2019)

statescsState self-control strategies

  • Description
  • Distribution
  • Statistics
  • Items
  • Values
  • Scale

Directions: “The following statements refer to your exercise-related goals. Please read each statement and indicate the extent to which it applies to your exercise goals.”

Variable Scale Prompt
statescs01 Planning "I make concrete plans for exercising (e.g., when, where, how, and with whom)."
statescs02 Habit "Exercise is something I do automatically (e.g., without thinking about it or having to remind myself)."
statescs03 Situation Modification "I create pleasant situations for exercising (e.g., choosing an attractive environment, exercising with others, varying activities)."
statescs04 Attention Deployment "I focus on specific aspects of exercising (e.g., proper movement execution) and ignore others (e.g., tempting alternatives)."
statescs05 Cognitive Change "I mentally prepare myself for exercising (e.g., focusing on positive effects, goals, and rewards, encouraging myself)."
statescs06 Response Modulation "I force myself to exercise (e.g., suppressing the impulse to do something else)."
statescs07 Emotion Regulation "I regulate my emotions (e.g., trying to stay in a good mood)."

1Does not apply at all 2Hardly applies 3Partly applies 4Mostly applies 5Fully applies

Variable Label Computation
